gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 1.5 V lithium AA they offer as the fix for voltage-sensitive devices has a protection circuit: XTAR says it 'will stop when the current exceeds 2-2.5A' and 'does not work on some camera flashes'. It also holds 1.5 V and then drops to 1.1 V instead of fading slowly. Separately, Kwikset says its smart-lock software is 'optimized for alkaline batteries', so rechargeables can show the wrong percentage and may not give 'correct low-battery warnings'.
standout_why: Compared against Digital Camera World (cited), the Which? sample page (cited) and GeekChamp's Eneloop vs LADDA page (rank 2). Digital Camera World only says Li-ion AAs give 'the full 1.5V output' for 'voltage-critical devices', with no current limit, flash caveat or gauge behaviour. Which? covers none of this. GeekChamp has part of it: some devices 'report a low battery early', a 1.5 V lithium is 'a targeted compatibility choice', and the charger must match. But it gives no current limit, no flash incompatibility, no output curve and nothing from a lock maker. ChatGPT's own answer only says voltage-sensitive devices 'may require rechargeable 1.5V lithium batteries'.
decides: This confirms Eneloop Pro (NiMH, no output-cutoff circuit) over the XTAR 1.5 V lithium for camera flashes, the use ChatGPT gave the Pro. XTAR itself says its cells cut out above 2-2.5 A and fail in some flashes. It also qualifies our XTAR row ('Smart locks, thermostats that misread NiMH'). The XTAR's flat 1.5 V followed by a step to 1.1 V near empty is not the alkaline-shaped decline Kwikset says its lock software expects. So the page should send lock owners to the lock maker's battery guidance first, and not present 1.5 V lithium as a guaranteed fix.

findings.label: Output cutoff current (protection circuit)
findings.value: Output stops above 2-2.5 A; XTAR advises against devices needing more than 2.5 A instantaneous or more than 2 A continuous
findings.source_title: FAQs about XTAR 4150mWh AA Li-ion Battery
findings.note: Maker's FAQ, quoted: 'The output will stop when the current exceeds 2-2.5A.' The cutoff does not damage the cell.

findings.label: Camera flash compatibility
findings.value: Maker says it 'does not work on some camera flashes'
findings.source_title: FAQs about XTAR 4150mWh AA Li-ion Battery
findings.note: XTAR's reason: flashes draw high instantaneous current, and repeated firing heats the cell until its protection trips.

findings.label: End-of-charge output behaviour
findings.value: Holds 1.5 V for about 78-85% of the discharge, then steps to 1.1 V (when the internal cell reaches about 3.15 V); averages 1.44 V
findings.source_title: AA Battery Test & Comparison: XTAR, Energizer, Duracell, GP (XTAR)
findings.note: Maker's own test at 200 mA: a stable 1.5 V for about 11 h of about 14 h total. The 3.15 V internal figure and the warning that below 1.1 V 'the device may interpret it as insufficient battery power' come from https://xtar.cc/?p=8567, read 2026-11-17. Maker-run test, not independent.

findings.label: Smart-lock maker guidance on rechargeable AAs (Kwikset)
findings.value: Not recommended: software and app 'optimized for alkaline batteries'; 'the displayed battery percentage may not be accurate'; user 'might not receive correct low-battery warnings'; rechargeables 'will not harm your smart lock'
findings.source_title: Can I use rechargeable batteries for my smart lock? | Kwikset Support
findings.note: Kwikset's support page. It does not say whether 1.5 V lithium rechargeables count as 'rechargeable' here; it recommends alkaline.

findings.label: Discharge voltage profile vs alkaline
findings.value: 'eneloop Ni-MH AA and AAA batteries maintain a consistent level of 1.2V power throughout the entire life of the charge'; alkaline is rated 1.5 V but 'the voltage rapidly drops below the NiMH rating of 1.2V'
findings.source_title: Consistent discharge performance | Panasonic Battery Products (Panasonic Energy Corporation of America)
findings.note: US Panasonic battery site (Columbus, GA address). This is why gauges calibrated to alkaline read NiMH as lower than it is. The page itself does not mention gauges.

unsourced: Panasonic's own FAQ wording that a device's battery indicator may show less remaining capacity on eneloop, and that devices are designed for 1.5 V to 0.9 V: all four regional FAQ pages (panasonic.com sg/ph/global/global consumer) returned HTTP 403, so it comes only from search snippets and is left out.

Schlage/Allegion statement that 'Lithium, rechargeable, and older battery technologies may cause undesirable operation', and the Schlage Home app note that lithium may 'fail to trigger low battery' notifications: kc.allegion.com returned 403 on WebFetch and curl was not approved.

XTAR datasheet figures (2 A max continuous, 1,200 cycles, 1.1 V low-power voltage): the Battery Junction datasheet PDF is image-only and not machine-readable, so they come only from a search snippet. The FAQ's 2-2.5 A cutoff is used instead.
Eneloop Pro's maximum discharge current and the current a typical speedlight draws on recycle: I didn't look further after hitting the call budget, and nothing is published on the pages I opened.
Yale and August lock battery guidance: not reached within the budget.
